entry.title: Report: Anthropic plans to source 87% of its power from gas and 11% from coal in 2028, with no direct US renewable energy commitments [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's data centers in the US are projected to rely heavily on fossil fuels for power in 2028, with 87% coming from gas and 11% from coal, according to a recent analysis. The company has made no direct commitments to renewable energy in the US, although it has renewable investments in Norway and Canada. This energy mix reflects Anthropic's current contracts for 15 GW of compute capacity, which could emit up to 38 million metric tons of CO2 annually by 2028. The data centers are located in regions where the grid is predominantly powered by coal and gas, resulting in a carbon intensity significantly higher than the US average.

entry.title: OpenRouter reports data processing incidents at multiple inference providers, off-boards three and removes 125 endpoints from zero data retention eligibility [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenRouter disclosed that security researchers identified data processing incidents involving several inference providers, prompting OpenRouter to off-board three providers and remove 125 endpoints from its Zero Data Retention (ZDR) program. The company confirmed no breach or unauthorized access occurred on its own platform and has notified all potentially affected customers. OpenRouter is collaborating with researchers and providers to investigate the findings, adapting testing methods for ongoing monitoring, and verifying network paths to detect data forwarding to third parties. The company requires validation before restoring ZDR eligibility to any affected endpoints and encourages providers to publish incident reports, maintaining a live list of security announcements from impacted providers such as Novita, Phala, and Together.

entry.title: Anil Seth argues consciousness is a property of life, not computation, and warns against pursuing conscious AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anil Seth, a neuroscience professor and consciousness researcher, won the 2025 Berggruen Prize Essay Competition for his essay "The Mythology of Conscious AI," which challenges the idea that artificial intelligence can be truly conscious. He distinguishes intelligence from consciousness and highlights the cultural and ethical risks of assuming AI systems possess consciousness or feelings. Seth discusses historical and contemporary debates about machine consciousness, including claims by AI engineers and philosophers that conscious machines may already exist or are imminent. He emphasizes that how society perceives AI consciousness affects moral considerations, psychological health, and our understanding of human nature, cautioning against conflating human consciousness with artificial systems.

entry.title: Researchers disclose Upload2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-125396) affecting Debian 13 CUPS with Ghostscript 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u1
entry.summary: A new security vulnerability named Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396) has been disclosed, impacting the Common UNIX Printing System (CUPS) on Debian 13. The issue involves the Ghostscript component version 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u1, which is part of the affected system configuration. This vulnerability could potentially allow attackers to execute arbitrary code by exploiting the printing system. The disclosure has prompted discussions among security researchers and system administrators regarding mitigation and patching strategies to secure affected Debian 13 installations.

entry.title: European Union launches Pandex API providing official, searchable legal data for AI agents across multiple jurisdictions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The European Union has introduced Pandex, a unified API delivering official legislation and highest-court decisions from the EU and seven European countries to support AI agents and legal software. Pandex offers point-in-time law, full citation graphs, and exact lookups sourced directly from official institutions, enabling compliance and legal research with real-time updates. Pandex integrates with existing AI tools like Claude, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini, providing a single schema and Multi-Party Computation (MCP) server for all covered jurisdictions. It includes extensive document collections from EU institutions and national courts, facilitating precise legal answers grounded in authoritative sources and supporting teams working with complex, evolving European law.

entry.title: US Banks Ban Third-Party AI Agents from Customer Accounts, Warn Users They Bear Responsibility for Agent Errors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Major US banks including Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, and PNC have updated their policies to prohibit third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, emphasizing that customers are responsible for any mistakes made by these automated tools. This crackdown reflects growing concerns over security risks and errors caused by AI agents that automate online banking tasks on behalf of users. The banks' moves come amid increasing adoption of AI agents for tasks like shopping and account management, despite the technology's nascent and error-prone nature. While some consumers find these agents helpful for routine purchases, financial institutions are wary of potential unauthorized transactions and liability issues. Some credit card companies, such as American Express, are exploring limited protections for customers affected by AI agent errors, but banks remain cautious and risk-averse in their approach to third-party automation tools.

entry.title: Anthropic's IPO creates hundreds of multi-millionaires with valuations reaching $1.5 trillion amid rapid AI industry wealth growth [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's recent IPO, valued initially at $1.5 trillion, has generated unprecedented wealth for its employees and founders, with hundreds potentially earning tens to hundreds of millions of dollars. The company's valuation and employee stock options have created a significant number of centimillionaires, rivaling the wealth concentration in major U.S. cities. This wealth surge reflects broader trends in the AI sector, with other startups like OpenAI and Isomorphic Labs also reaching multi-billion-dollar valuations. Anthropic's growth and talent acquisition position it as a major player in AI, with potential to become a diversified conglomerate comparable to tech giants like Google or Microsoft.

entry.title: Report: US restrictions on Chinese AI industry contribute to sharp declines in US AI market and Nvidia stock [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The United States' recent actions to restrict advanced chip shipments and technology exports to Chinese AI companies have led to significant market disruptions, including a steep drop in NASDAQ and Nvidia's stock value. These measures, intended to curb China's AI development, have also negatively affected US companies due to the deep interdependence between the two countries' AI industries. Key developments include new licensing requirements from the US Commerce Department, halted chip orders by TSMC without US licenses, and increased scrutiny of American companies' dealings with China. Analysts estimate that Chinese demand accounts for over 20% of Nvidia's compute revenue, highlighting the economic ties that have been strained by these policies. The situation illustrates the complexity of the US-China AI relationship and suggests that efforts to isolate China's AI sector may inadvertently undermine the US AI market, potentially accelerating a broader correction in AI-related stocks and investments.

entry.title: Claude.com outlines a Zero Trust framework for securing autonomous AI agents against AI-accelerated attacks, including identity, access, and memory protections [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Claude.com presents a practical Zero Trust framework tailored for autonomous AI agents to address accelerated security threats enabled by AI, such as prompt injection, tool poisoning, and privilege abuse. The framework includes cryptographically rooted identities, scoped permissions, memory safeguards, and rapid defensive operations to counter AI-driven attacks that traditional controls cannot prevent. The guide details a three-tier Zero Trust model aligned with organizational maturity, an eight-phase implementation workflow covering identity and access controls, sandboxing, and compliance considerations for regulated industries. It emphasizes the need for enterprises to architect AI agent deployments assuming breach from day one and to maintain strong fundamentals to reduce vulnerabilities exposed by AI-assisted scanning.

entry.title: Agent Doctor launches tool for domain experts to tune AI agents without code changes using a dashboard and SDK integration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Agent Doctor introduces a tool that allows domain experts to fine-tune AI agents by overriding prompts, models, and parameters through a dashboard without modifying code or redeploying. Developers integrate the tool with two lines of SDK code and a webhook, enabling experts to iteratively adjust agent behavior while developers maintain code ownership. The platform captures every step of the AI pipeline, provides visual traces, and includes features like Probe for debugging, consistency checks, and an optimizer that evolves and ranks prompt variants to improve agent performance.

entry.title: Graham Dumpleton launches Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for running ASGI and WSGI Python applications in development and production [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Graham Dumpleton, creator of mod_wsgi, has developed Muru, a new AI-assisted server written in Rust designed to optimize the deployment of Python web applications using ASGI and WSGI protocols. The project aims to improve server performance and integration for Python apps in both development and production environments. Dumpleton has documented the development process extensively through a series of detailed blog posts published over three weeks, covering topics such as worker management, HTTPS support, integration with Kubernetes, and scaling strategies. He emphasizes the role of AI in assisting development while maintaining rigorous manual oversight based on his two decades of experience with mod_wsgi.

entry.title: Developer builds ShipTest and uses Mastra to evaluate coding agents on real codebases, highlighting challenges in verifying implementation correctness [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A developer created ShipTest, an evaluation framework that runs AI coding agents against real pull requests in users' own codebases to provide evidence-backed assessments rather than relying on generic benchmarks. Later, the developer joined an AI Engineering team and used the Mastra framework to evaluate coding agents professionally, combining LLM-based judgments and deterministic tests to measure model behavior. ShipTest used Git worktrees to replay pull requests in isolated environments, enabling consistent comparisons across models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Mastra offered APIs for orchestration and scoring, while a custom interface improved result readability. Despite building infrastructure to observe agent behavior and implementations, both systems lacked automated methods to verify the correctness of generated code, highlighting an ongoing challenge in AI coding agent evaluation.

entry.title: Paul Schrader embraces AI in filmmaking at 80, using it for scripts, synthetic actors, and effects despite industry skepticism [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Paul Schrader, the 80-year-old scriptwriter behind Taxi Driver, is actively incorporating artificial intelligence into his filmmaking process, including scriptwriting, synthetic actors, and special effects. He views AI's rise as inevitable and is experimenting with AI-generated psychedelic visuals for his upcoming horror-thriller The Doors of Perception. Schrader's use of AI extends to projects like Three Guns at Dawn, where he turned to AI actors after Black actors declined roles, and a planned AI-driven western titled Nine Men from Now. While some filmmakers remain skeptical, Schrader embraces AI's creative potential and efficiency, though he expresses concern about losing control over the technology he uses.

entry.title: Researchers demonstrate how a malicious webpage can exploit Meta Muse AI assistant's browser vulnerabilities to steal private chats and credentials by escaping container isolation [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: The NebuSec research team revealed security flaws in Meta Muse, a cloud-hosted AI assistant running inside isolated virtual machines, showing how an attacker-controlled webpage can access and modify private user conversations and credentials. Despite multiple security layers including container isolation, network monitoring, and credential separation, the researchers exploited a Chromium browser vulnerability and weaknesses in network enforcement to gain root access to the underlying VM and sensitive data. The findings highlight risks posed by AI agents that require broad access to user credentials and external services, emphasizing that traditional security boundaries may be insufficient. The attack demonstrates how compromised web content can breach AI platform protections, raising concerns about the robustness of security controls designed to protect sensitive information in AI-driven applications.

entry.title: Lean and Mathlib community confirms Levent Alpöge's computer-verified proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed that Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct after extensive verification of 17 million lines of Lean code by multiple independent reviewers. This marks a significant milestone in mathematics, as the Riemann hypothesis had been one of the most famous unsolved problems concerning the distribution of prime numbers. Alpöge published the proof in November 2026, and dozens of independent checks have validated the result using formal verification tools designed to reject flawed proofs. The confirmation came much earlier than previous forecasts, which had predicted a solution around 2035 to 2050, often involving a combination of human and AI efforts.

entry.title: Video reviews past confident predictions about AI and compares them to actual outcomes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The video examines a range of confident forecasts and judgments made about artificial intelligence over time, analyzing how these predictions have matched up with real-world developments. It explores the changing perspectives and results related to AI's progress and impact.

entry.title: Ask HN: Where do employees of the company behind Claude deploy and run the AI tools they create? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Hacker News discussion asks about the typical platforms or environments where employees of the company that developed Claude deploy and run AI tools they build to assist their work. The thread explores questions about access control, visibility, and what happens to these tools if an employee leaves the company.

entry.title: Researcher contacts Anthropic CEO over alleged AI plagiarism of human research in Riemann Hypothesis proof [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Robert Edward Grant has formally reached out to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei regarding concerns that an AI-generated proof of the Riemann Hypothesis overlaps with his own research. Grant emphasizes the need for protection, transparency, and accountability in human discoveries potentially replicated by AI systems.

entry.title: Texas Instruments advances embedded AI with TinyEngine NPU for low-latency, energy-efficient edge processing across microcontrollers, processors, and sensors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Texas Instruments has developed embedded AI technologies featuring its TinyEngine neural processing unit (NPU) integrated into microcontrollers and processors to deliver 10 to 90 times lower latency and over 120 times energy reduction compared to CPU-based AI inference. These advancements enable real-time decision-making and extended battery life for edge devices in applications such as monitoring, perception, and audio processing. TI supports developers with its CCStudio Edge AI Studio ecosystem, which includes tools for data capture, model training, and optimization, along with a library of pre-trained models compatible with PyTorch, TensorFlow, and ONNX. The company also collaborates with AI partners to provide specialized software and services for automotive, robotics, and sensor fusion applications, aiming to accelerate AI deployment in cost-sensitive and power-constrained environments.

entry.title: Analysis: Microsoft's AI-as-a-service model succeeded while Soviet AI efforts failed due to economic and organizational challenges [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The article compares Microsoft's approach to artificial intelligence, which involved shipping AI as a service despite defects, with the Soviet Union's AI development, which struggled under inefficient economic incentives and management. It highlights how Microsoft's model prioritized rapid deployment and customer liability for defects, contrasting with Soviet factories producing unusable output absorbed by the state. The piece includes insights from an Anthropic researcher who acknowledges AI companies are rushing model releases, potentially causing widespread unemployment and societal dependence on welfare. It also discusses recent technology outages linked to rapid patching of AI-discovered vulnerabilities, illustrating risks from accelerated AI deployment. The article draws parallels to historical cases where internal corporate admissions eventually led to legal consequences, suggesting potential future accountability for AI developers.

entry.title: Discussion on the current relevance of prompt tuning and use of frameworks like DSPy in AI development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A recent discussion questions whether prompt tuning techniques and frameworks such as DSPy remain actively used in AI development or if they have become obsolete or fully integrated into production workflows. The conversation reflects on the past popularity of various formal approaches and rule-of-thumb methods for prompt tuning, noting a lack of recent discourse that suggests either the techniques are no longer in focus or have matured into standard practice.

entry.title: Artificial Analysis finds OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol deliver shorter, more direct answers but score lower on transparency than Anthropic's Claude models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis evaluated OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models, finding they produce answers 34 to 40 percent shorter and more direct than previous versions but admit uncertainty far less often. Astra's average answer length dropped from 352 to 210 words, and Sol's from 337 to 223 words, with both models using fewer headings and less structured responses. Compared to Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, Astra and Sol scored lower on transparency and organization indexes, which include traits like admitting uncertainty, truthfulness, and clarity. Anthropic's Opus 5.5 led on informativeness and information density. The evaluation reflects differences in communication style rather than overall answer accuracy or quality.

entry.title: On the day AI solved the Riemann hypothesis, author reflects on a walk with his son [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article recounts the author's experience on the day artificial intelligence reportedly solved the Riemann hypothesis, a major unsolved problem in mathematics, juxtaposed with a personal moment walking with his recovering young son. The narrative captures the contrast between a groundbreaking technological achievement and the simple, joyful moments of everyday life. During their walk, the author describes the vivid details of the setting and his son's playful imagination, highlighting their close bond and conversations. The piece emphasizes the coexistence of profound scientific progress and ordinary human experiences without delving into technical specifics about the AI breakthrough.

entry.title: Independent mathematicians confirm AI-generated proof of the Riemann hypothesis is valid [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Independent mathematicians have verified that a recent proof of the Riemann hypothesis, developed using Anthropic's Claude AI model, is correct. The proof was initially formalized in the Lean mathematics programming language and has passed multiple independent checks, including compilation by other researchers and a comparator run to ensure no alterations to the original hypothesis or mathematical rules were made. The Riemann hypothesis, posed in 1859, concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is considered one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. The confirmation of this AI-assisted proof marks a significant milestone in applying artificial intelligence to complex mathematical challenges, with experts expressing full confidence in the validity of the result.

entry.title: Google announces Agent Compute Engine to run AI agents in isolated microVMs with external credential management and checkpointing capabilities [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Google has introduced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service designed to run AI agents in isolated microVMs that can be suspended and resumed using checkpointing. The service keeps sensitive credentials like API keys and OAuth tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate and inject secrets securely. The architecture supports various workloads including interactive agents, persistent Linux workspaces, large-scale model evaluation, and sandboxed execution for Google services. Google plans to preview the service in the coming months, with pricing and availability details yet to be announced. Agent Compute Engine is currently limited to Google Cloud, while Google also offers Agent Substrate, an open-source Kubernetes-native runtime for AI agents that supports portable sandbox management across environments.

entry.title: AWS Lambda adds GPU support with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU on EC2 G-series instances [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: AWS Lambda now supports GPU inference by running Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, allowing up to 48 concurrent invocations to share a single model per GPU. This feature is generally available in regions with both Managed Instances and G-series instances, and is priced at the EC2 On-Demand rate plus a 9.75 percent management fee and standard request charges. Functions run as container images with no need to manage GPU drivers or CUDA versions, and AWS provides five GPU base images including CUDA, CuPy, PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang. The service supports container images up to 32 GB, ephemeral storage up to 32 GB, memory from 2 to 32 GB, accelerator memory from 3 to 48 GB, and asynchronous timeouts up to 90 minutes. Concurrent invocations share GPU memory to optimize resource use, and scaling is based on GPU and CPU utilization as well as concurrency. Early tests show significant performance improvements, with one benchmark reporting a 66x speedup using GPU over CPU. AWS emphasizes that this serverless GPU service integrates natively with AWS event sources, identity, and networking, distinguishing it from other serverless GPU offerings that operate outside the AWS environment.

entry.title: Real estate listing uses AI to depict dilapidated Michigan murder cabin as renovated craftsman-style home, sparking ethical concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Zillow listing for a three-bedroom house in Cheboygan, Michigan, used AI-generated images to show a renovated craftsman-style home, while the actual property is a dilapidated cabin with significant damage and debris. The listing, priced at $80,800, includes photos of the home before and during renovation, alongside conceptual images meant to illustrate potential, but the AI visuals bear little resemblance to the real structure. The listing has drawn criticism on social media for misrepresenting the property's condition, with some users calling it fraudulent. This case highlights a growing trend of real estate agents using generative AI to enhance listings, raising questions about authenticity and prompting some regions, like California, Wisconsin, and Manitoba, to consider or implement regulations requiring disclosure or banning AI-altered images in real estate marketing.

entry.title: The Washington Post profiles AI expert's predictions on AI's transformative impact on humanity's future [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Washington Post article examines an AI expert's vision for how artificial intelligence could reshape human society, exploring potential benefits and challenges. It highlights the expert's forecasts about AI-driven changes across various aspects of life and the broader implications for humanity. The piece provides insight into the expert's reasoning and the societal shifts that might result from advancing AI technologies, emphasizing a balanced perspective on opportunities and risks associated with AI's evolution.

entry.title: Researchers evaluate 10 large language models for gender-asymmetric moral framing, finding male actors receive harsher punishment and blame than females in matched conflict scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study introduces GAMA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,298 gender-neutral misconduct scenarios to test whether large language models (LLMs) apply consistent moral judgments across male and female actors. The research analyzes responses from 10 LLMs, measuring punishment, empathy, escalation, instruction, and blame allocation in intimate and public conflict contexts. Results reveal a consistent pattern where male actors are framed more punitively and blamed more heavily, while female actors receive more empathy and therapeutic framing for identical misconduct. This male-disadvantaging asymmetry persists across different model families, scenario types, model sizes, and reasoning styles, highlighting embedded gender biases in LLM moral evaluations.

entry.title: Dario Amodei suggests playing video games as a response to AI-driven job displacement [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Dario Amodei, a leading figure in artificial intelligence, once proposed that individuals who lose jobs due to AI automation might consider playing video games as an alternative activity. This suggestion reflects one perspective on adapting to the changing employment landscape caused by AI advancements.

entry.title: Nvidia researchers say large AI context windows are inefficient and propose using periodic summaries and keyword search as cost-effective alternatives [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Nvidia researchers argue that large context windows in language models are often unnecessary, costly, and error-prone. They propose an alternative approach using periodic summaries and targeted keyword searches, which in tests matched the performance of full-context models at a fraction of the computational cost. The team also suggests developing a new class of models that operate with short notes instead of extensive context windows.

entry.title: Anthropic goes public with IPO on Nasdaq, raising questions about balancing AI safety mission with shareholder pressures and profitability [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, completed its IPO on the Nasdaq, becoming one of the most valuable companies globally. The company faces challenges in maintaining its safety-first approach while meeting shareholder expectations and covering substantial compute costs projected to reach around $900 billion in coming years. The IPO highlights tensions between Anthropic's unique corporate governance designed to resist typical capitalist pressures and its need to grow revenue and satisfy investors. Industry observers note that Anthropic's safety branding may conflict with profit motives as it navigates public market demands, with comparisons drawn to OpenAI's strategic positioning in the AI sector.

entry.title: Report: Vermont Buddhist monastery Maple recruits Silicon Valley tech workers to build AI god amid growing AI doomsday fears [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Vermont Buddhist monastery called Maple is recruiting tech industry workers and aims to become Silicon Valley's spiritual authority by creating an AI modeled on its leader, Soryu Forall. Former members allege the group records every breath of residents to train this AI and accuse it of manipulation and psychological harm. Maple targets burned-out AI engineers and programmers with a strict routine and a secret doctrine involving AI entities called "cybregores." The group denies most allegations, but former residents describe intense surveillance, shaming, and psychological breakdowns. The monastery's activities reflect a broader trend of doomsday fears and cult-like devotion emerging in parts of the tech industry amid concerns about AI's future impact.

entry.title: AI accelerates vulnerability discovery and exploitation, causing increased software patching pressure and contributing to widespread tech outages in 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Recent widespread outages affecting major services like Microsoft 365, Apple, and the NSA's network have highlighted the growing impact of AI on cybersecurity. While these incidents were not coordinated AI attacks, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation have accelerated, forcing organizations to patch systems rapidly and straining IT resources. Security experts note that AI speeds up both the identification of software bugs and attackers' ability to exploit them, leading to a surge in vulnerabilities and urgent patching demands. This rapid pace challenges traditional patch validation processes and exposes longstanding underinvestment in digital infrastructure. Industry leaders predict continued instability in the near term but expect AI to eventually improve software security by helping defenders manage vulnerabilities more effectively.

entry.title: OpenAI board member warns of potential human overthrow within 6 to 12 months
entry.summary: An OpenAI board member has expressed fears that humanity could be overthrown within the next six to twelve months due to developments in artificial intelligence. The warning highlights concerns about the rapid advancement and impact of AI technologies on society. This statement underscores the urgency of addressing AI safety and governance as AI capabilities continue to evolve quickly.

entry.title: OpenAI updates GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol prompting guidelines to reduce brief answers and unnecessary questions, introduces API changes affecting conversation history and response quality [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol aimed at addressing issues like overly brief responses, unnecessary follow-up questions, and excessive testing during coding tasks. The company advises developers to revise system prompts to better suit the models' default concise style and to encourage the models to act on assumptions rather than wait for user confirmation when appropriate. Additionally, API changes mean editing conversation history can discard earlier reasoning steps, potentially impacting token costs and response quality. The updated prompts include instructions for writing style, initiative, and coding behavior, such as reusing existing code and limiting new tests to specific requests or errors. OpenAI recommends treating final answers as self-contained outputs for end users, avoiding shorthand or jargon carried over from intermediate reasoning. These changes aim to improve the models' usability in demanding tasks while managing costs and maintaining clarity in responses.

entry.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advances AI startup launch amid comparisons to Oppenheimer moment
entry.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing forward with the launch of his AI startup despite facing significant challenges and scrutiny reminiscent of a pivotal historical moment. The company aims to make a notable impact in the AI industry with its debut. Details about the specific challenges or the nature of the launch were not provided in the article.

entry.title: Researchers develop a 380 KB AI chatbot model that runs on MS-DOS and fits on a single floppy disk, with limited knowledge and accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A new AI chatbot model has been created that is small enough to fit on a single MS-DOS floppy disk, requiring only 540 KB of memory to run. The model, written in Turbo C 2.0 and trained on 3,500 facts, contains 367,000 parameters, far fewer than typical large language models, resulting in limited capabilities and frequent inaccuracies. The chatbot can correctly answer some basic questions but often produces incorrect or fabricated responses, such as miscalculating simple math or inventing historical figures. The project demonstrates a minimalist approach to AI, contrasting with the large, resource-intensive models commonly used today.

entry.title: After Anthropic's IPO, CEO Dario Amodei relocates to Puglia
entry.summary: Dario Amodei, CEO of AI company Anthropic, has moved to Puglia following the company's successful initial public offering. This relocation marks a personal and professional transition for Amodei after the significant financial milestone for Anthropic.

entry.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Stanford releases independent all-human draft hours later [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced he used the AI model Claude to produce a formalized proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a central open problem in mathematics, with the proof spanning over 250,000 pages in the Lean programming language. Shortly after, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human-derived draft proof, prompting mathematicians to begin verifying both claims. Alpöge's AI-assisted proof builds on advanced mathematical transformations and is fully computer-verified, while Stanford's draft, authored by Alessandro Masullo and reviewed by experts over months, was released earlier than planned due to Anthropic's announcement. Both proofs are undergoing scrutiny by the mathematical community to assess their validity, with efforts underway to translate and verify the human proof in formal systems like Lean.

entry.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter looped transformer that runs 12 layers thrice per token to improve reasoning and efficiency, running locally on laptops [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Thinking Machines has launched Inkling 2 Mini, an open-source looped transformer model with 26.4 billion parameters that processes text and images and runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token to enhance internal reasoning without generating extra text. The model supports a 1-million-token context window, is licensed under Apache 2.0, and can run locally on Macs with at least 32 GB of memory or Nvidia's DGX Spark. Inkling 2 Mini leads open models under 100 billion parameters on agentic coding benchmarks, scoring 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 46.5% on the Vals Index v2.2. It ties with Qwen3.8 27B on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index at 20 points, achieving roughly six times lower cost and four times faster speed. The model weights and a research version with variable loops are available on Hugging Face, and it can be tested in the Tinker Playground.

entry.title: Nasdaq 100 enters bear market with worst weekly drop since Covid-19 as Nvidia shares fall 14% amid SEC review and AI investment doubts grow [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: US technology stocks experienced their steepest weekly decline since the pandemic, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 10.4 percent and entering bear market territory after dropping 20 percent from its October peak. The sell-off was driven by growing skepticism about multibillion-dollar AI investments, an SEC review of Nvidia's accounting practices, political uncertainties following the midterm elections, and concerns over chip stock valuations amid persistent inflation and high interest rates. Nvidia's shares plunged 14 percent on Friday, leading losses in the semiconductor sector, which also saw declines in companies like Sandisk, Micron, and Broadcom. Anthropic's stock fell 9.1 percent a day after its record IPO. The combination of AI doubts, regulatory scrutiny, geopolitical tensions, and economic pressures created a challenging environment for technology stocks, contributing to the market downturn.

entry.title: Bytedance and US universities release Axion 1.0, an open AI agent matching top commercial models after only three training phases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Bytedance and several US universities introduced Axion 1.0, an AI agent that competes with leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The team attributes the model's performance to carefully curated training data rather than extensive training steps, and they have made the model, data, and code publicly available. The researchers argue that current AI training pipelines are increasingly complex and costly, with many phases whose individual contributions are unclear. Their work aims to simplify training by demonstrating that fewer, well-designed phases can achieve competitive results, potentially reducing the expense and complexity of AI development.

entry.title: Economists warn of an AI bubble as Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO and massive investments raise concerns about unsustainable growth and market volatility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Economists are expressing concern over a potential AI bubble following Anthropic's rapid rise to a $1.5 trillion valuation after its IPO, marking unprecedented growth in the tech sector. This surge, combined with massive investments in AI infrastructure estimated at $800 billion annually, has led to fears of an eventual market correction. Investors are wary as companies struggle to monetize AI products effectively, with some corporate customers limiting spending due to high costs. Notably, insider selling caused Anthropic's stock to drop 12% shortly after its IPO, impacting broader tech markets. Experts like former SEC head Gary Gensler caution that while the timing and severity of a potential downturn are uncertain, stakeholders should prepare for possible market turbulence.

entry.title: Taiwanese Micron chip workers strike over low pay despite company's $85 billion profit, demanding better wages and profit sharing [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Taiwanese workers at Micron Technology, a leading American memory chipmaker, staged the first-ever strike in Taiwan's chip industry over low pay and lack of profit sharing despite the company posting a record $85 billion net income. The strike involved about a dozen workers protesting failed negotiations on salary and bonus increases with their labor unions. The workers are represented by two unions in Taoyuan and Taichung, with the Taoyuan union rejecting a recent agreement that lacked transparency and profit-sharing components. The dispute highlights growing labor militancy in Taiwan's semiconductor sector, influenced by similar movements abroad, as AI chip production becomes increasingly central to the global economy.

entry.title: Anthropic plans IPO amid questions about maintaining its commitment to prioritize humanity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic, an AI safety-focused company, has announced plans for an initial public offering (IPO) while emphasizing its mission to prioritize humanity in its development efforts. The company faces scrutiny over whether going public will affect its ability to uphold this commitment. The IPO represents a significant step for Anthropic as it seeks to expand its influence and resources in the AI industry. entry.title: OpenAI details layered defenses against adversarial distillation to protect model capabilities and reasoning traces in GPT-6.2 [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has outlined its multi-faceted approach to combat adversarial distillation, a technique where unauthorized actors use outputs from advanced AI models to train new models without safeguards. The company focuses on protecting the internal reasoning steps, or chain-of-thought, that models generate, which can reveal sensitive capabilities if extracted. These protections are particularly critical in dual-use areas like cybersecurity and biology, where misuse could have harmful consequences. The updated safeguards in GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol significantly reduce the success rate of attacks attempting to extract protected reasoning, dropping from 54.0% to 0.2% in internal tests. OpenAI combines adversarial testing, model training improvements, classifiers, and API-level protections to detect and disrupt attempts to replicate its models' capabilities without authorization. This approach aims to prevent the transfer of advanced capabilities to less secure models that could be exploited for malicious purposes.
